deck: The Victoria's Secret Fashion Show streamed on Sunday and the audience data landed this morning.  Streams Charts puts it in the year's ten most popular non-sports livestreams, which is rare company for a brand's own channel, and the two decisions that preceded it both cut against how owned video normally gets planned. tldr: Victoria's Secret held 3.14 million people on its own YouTube channel at once on Sunday and lifted the event's total peak 32.9 percent on last year, having first run a reality series on the same channel and consolidated the broadcast from several platforms onto one — so fund the serialised content in the weeks before your next tentpole and pick a single platform for the stream.

Glossy's new index has paid creator posts averaging 334,055 views against 48,008 for gifted, and puts the gap down to the media budget behind one of them — so report paid and gifted reach in separate columns with the amplification spend named, and stop adding the two totals together.

Inside paid creator posts the styled shot averaged 707,646 views and the product demonstration 250,764, while among gifted posts the demonstration was the best format — so brief your next paid creator post as a styled video and move your demonstrations to your own channel and your gifting programme.

On 28 October Meta switches product browsing on by default in ads that are already running, putting a page with personalised suggestions between your paid click and your website, based on a 3 percent average conversion gain it has not explained — so decide before the 28th, opt out wherever the landing page is doing specific work, and record the date.

Certified online gambling advertisers can buy the YouTube homepage banner from tomorrow, and brand suitability controls cannot exclude it because you are not buying the adjacency — so get your Google representative to confirm in writing which markets are live and what controls exist.

Streams Charts found the organiser's own channels carried 99.4 percent of La Velada's hours watched and 3.7 percent of Z Event's, on events whose headline hours-watched figures look comparable — so require average concurrents, airtime, and the share of hours carried by your specific placement on every live proposal.

Spotify launched paid podcast memberships in 34 markets at a 90 percent revenue share with fewer adverts as a sellable perk — so ask every podcast proposal whether a members tier exists, what it removes, and what share of listening sits behind it, and price on ad-supported listening rather than total listening.

One narrowed the distribution.  The other spent the money before the event rather than on it.
